Turn 50: Best valid = 1.474 (feed '' 36/2.6/2.6/0.8 -> T worthless; B 36/4.0/4.0/0.8 -> BT = C6-paraffin mix $1060.6M/yr; BB worthless; total column cost $414M/yr). Reverted to clear the loss-making T column (turn 49 gave -0.346).

All 4 island peers (R1803, R1997, R2007, R2009) converged on the identical 1.474 two-column design; nothing better found in 48 solves by anyone. Confirmed failures: taller/higher-reflux T column (turns 45,47) -> negative, because T's condenser must knock down C3 (propylene/propane ~18%), forcing refrigeration that costs ~$800M/yr, far exceeding any C5-mix revenue (~$620M). Cheaper feed column (R2007) or taller B (R1895) both worse.

Conclusion: T (1587 mol/s; C3 18% + C4 34% + C5 44%) is unseparable at a profit — its volatility range needs a very cold condenser. BB (nC7/nC8/cyclohexane/nonane mix) needs sharp cuts between close boilers, also unprofitable. The C6-paraffin blend BT (2-methylpentane+3-methylpentane+2,2-dimethylbutane+n-hexane, 95%+) is the only money-maker. 1.474 is the optimum; finished.
